newsitem.title: UK: Mobil says sells gas via Interconnector to enduser.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says sells gas via Interconnector to enduser.

text.p: Mobil Europe Gas Inc (MEGAS), a unit of U.S. oil giant Mobil Corp, said on Wednesday it had agreed the first sale of gas via the Interconnector direct to an enduser in Europe.
At the same time, MEGAS said it had become the first non-equity holder to secure capacity in the Interconnector pipeline, linking Bacton on the east coast of England with Zeebrugge in Belgium.
Mobil said from late 1998 it would supply Norsk Hydro Agri's Sluiskil plant in southern Holland with up to 2.2 million cubic metres per day of gas over a 15-year period.
For the lifetime of the Norsk Hydro contract, Mobil has negotiated access to 800 million cubic metres per year of Interconnector pipeline capacity.

"This agreement demonstrates that industry is spearheading the integration of Europe's diverse gas market and reinforces MEGAS's position as one of Europe's major players," said MEGAS President Axel Commichau.
All other sales via the Interconnector so far have been to wholesalers.

The 150-mile subsea pipeline is due to start transportation of gas in 1998. It will be the first direct gas pipeline connection between Britain and mainland Europe and will further integrate Europe's natural gas grid.
